# Kiln

> Isolated Linux microVMs on one host. A sandbox boots from a template snapshot in under a second, forks into copies, sleeps, and serves a port on a public hostname.

Authenticate every call with `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. A key names one tenant, and a call only ever reaches that tenant's rows.

## Machine readable

- [OpenAPI](https://api.example.com/openapi.json): every route, body and error code.
- [MCP](https://api.example.com/mcp): the same operations as tools, over Streamable HTTP.
- [Catalog](https://api.example.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json): this index, in one file.
- [Full documentation](https://api.example.com/llms-full.txt): every operation with its fields.

## The shortest path to a running sandbox

1. `POST /v1/templates` builds a template from an OCI image. `name`, `image`, `vcpus`, `memory_mb`, `disk_mb` and `egress_allow` are required; an empty `egress_allow` allows no egress. It answers 202 and builds after the answer.
2. `GET /v1/templates/{name}` until `state` is `ready`.
3. `POST /v1/sandboxes` restores that template into a sandbox. `template`, `lifecycle` (`ephemeral` or `persistent`) and `idle_seconds` are required.
4. `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/exec` runs a command. Send `Accept: text/event-stream` to read output as it runs.
5. `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/publish` serves a guest port on a public hostname.
6. `DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}` destroys it. Nothing is left behind.

`GET /v1/events` is a server-sent event stream that never ends. It starts at the latest event; send `?after=0` to replay every event of this tenant, and `?sandbox_id=` to keep one sandbox.

## Showing your work: a preview URL

An agent that changed an application can prove it runs, and hand a person a link instead of a diff.

1. Build the application image and push it to your registry. Kiln does not build application images.
2. Store the registry credential once with `POST /v1/registries`. The host pulls with it; the sandbox never holds it, because the sandbox runs the code under review.
3. `POST /v1/templates` with that image, an `egress_allow` list naming every host the application needs, and `ttl_seconds` so the preview ends even if nobody comes back for it.
4. `POST /v1/sandboxes` with `lifecycle: persistent`, an `idle_seconds` deadline, and `metadata` naming the change: the branch, the pull request, the commit. The metadata is how you find this preview again.
5. `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/publish` returns the URL. Give that to the person.

The preview sleeps after its idle deadline and wakes on the next request, so an open review costs nothing while nobody is looking. The host deletes the template at its TTL with the sandbox and the snapshot, so a forgotten preview cleans itself up.

Egress is deny by default. A preview that reaches a database or an API needs those hostnames in `egress_allow`, and nothing else is reachable from inside it.

## Credentials

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/credentials` binds a credential to one exact host. A request from the sandbox to that host leaves with the header that Kiln sets, and the value never enters the guest, so the sandbox forks and restores with no `allow_secret_fork`. A fork or a restore starts with no binding and takes its own `credentials` list.

- The guard terminates TLS only on a bound host. A client with a pinned certificate or a fixed root list fails there, and that caller keeps `env`.
- A provider-scoped key is stronger than a `path` prefix, because provider routing can differ from the prefix.
- Kiln does not scrub responses, because a scrub misses an encoded value. Do not bind a host that echoes headers.
- A CLI that refuses to start without a key takes a placeholder in `env`, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY=placeholder`. The guard replaces the header on the wire.
- A template built before this feature answers `conflict`. Build it again.

## The kiln command

`kiln` is the client for Linux and macOS. It reads `KILN_URL` and `KILN_API_KEY`, and has one command for each operation below. `--json` prints JSON, and `kiln init` writes the Kiln skill and the MCP entry into a repository.

The work loop for a preview environment is `kiln preview up --image X --port N`, which prints the URL, then `kiln logs <id>` when it fails, and `kiln preview down` when it is finished.

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success. |
| 1 | An API or network failure, or a template that did not build. |
| 2 | A usage or configuration error, such as a missing KILN_URL. |
| 3 | The API answered `not_found`. |
| 4 | The API answered `conflict`. |
| 5 | The API answered `exhausted`: a cap of this tenant is reached. |
| 6 | The API answered `invalid`. |
| 14 | `--timeout` ended the wait. The build continues. |
| 124 | `kiln exec`: the command reached `timeout_seconds`. |
| 125 | `kiln exec`: Kiln itself failed. Any other code from `kiln exec` is the exit code of the command. |

## Errors

Every error is `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}`. The code is stable: `invalid`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `exhausted`, `internal`. `exhausted` answers 429 and means a cap of this tenant is reached; the message names the cap. `not_found` also covers a row of another tenant.

## Operations

### events

`GET /v1/events`

`kiln events`

Read the event stream of this tenant as server-sent events. The stream starts at the latest event and never ends; ?after=0 replays every event, ?after=<id> continues from one, and ?sandbox_id= keeps one sandbox.

This call can stream. Read the body as it arrives.

Query:

- `after` (integer): Event id to continue after. Zero replays every event.
- `sandbox_id` (string): Keep the events of one sandbox.

Answers 200 with `EventList`.

### health

`GET /v1/health`

`kiln health`

Report whether the host can run sandboxes.

Answers 200 with `Health`.

### listRegistries

`GET /v1/registries`

`kiln registries list`

List the registry credentials of this tenant. The tokens are never returned.

Answers 200 with `RegistryList`.

### putRegistry

`POST /v1/registries`

`kiln registries put`

Store the credential a template build uses to pull a private image for this tenant.

Body:

- `host` (string, required): Registry hostname, such as ghcr.io.
- `username` (string, required): Username the registry accepts.
- `token` (string, required): Token or password. It is never returned.

Answers 201 with `Registry`.

### deleteRegistry

`DELETE /v1/registries/{host}`

`kiln registries delete`

Remove one registry credential.

Path:

- `host` (string): Registry hostname.

Answers 204 with no body.

### listSandboxes

`GET /v1/sandboxes`

`kiln sandboxes list`

List the sandboxes of this tenant.

Answers 200 with `SandboxList`.

### createSandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes`

`kiln sandboxes create`

Create a sandbox by restoring a template snapshot.

Body:

- `template` (string, required): Template the sandbox restores from.
- `lifecycle` (string, required): ephemeral or persistent. An ephemeral sandbox is destroyed at idle_seconds of no activity; a persistent one sleeps then and wakes on the next request.
- `ttl_seconds` (integer): Seconds until the sandbox is destroyed, whatever its activity. Null is no deadline.
- `idle_seconds` (integer, required): Seconds of no activity until an ephemeral sandbox is destroyed or a persistent one sleeps. Must be greater than zero.
- `metadata` (object): Free-form labels the caller reads back.
- `secrets` (array of string): Names of host secrets to inject.
- `env` (object): Environment variables for the start command, exec and the terminal. Every value is handled like the host secrets: it reaches guest memory only and is never returned. A key must not also be in secrets.

Answers 201 with `Sandbox`.

### deleteSandbox

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}`

`kiln sandboxes delete`

Destroy a sandbox and retire its hostnames.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 204 with no body.

### getSandbox

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}`

`kiln sandboxes get`

Read one sandbox with its published ports.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 200 with `Sandbox`.

### setCredentials

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/credentials`

`kiln sandboxes set-credentials`

Replace the credential bindings of one sandbox. A request from the sandbox to a bound host leaves with the header that Kiln sets, and the value never enters the guest. A value is never returned. A rotation is a new call. A sleeping sandbox takes the change without a wake. A template built before credential bindings answers conflict and must be rebuilt.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `credentials` (array of object, required): At most 16 bindings: name, host (one exact name that egress_allow covers), header, value, and optional path (a prefix) and methods. A request that does not match leaves with no key and with that header removed. An empty list removes every binding.

Answers 200 with `Sandbox`.

### setEgress

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/egress`

`kiln sandboxes set-egress`

Replace the egress policy of one sandbox. Send egress_allow or observe. The answer comes after the host swaps the policy and cuts every connection the guest opened. A connection to a published port stays. A sleeping sandbox takes the change without a wake, and a later snapshot or fork carries it.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `egress_allow` (array of string): Hostnames the sandbox may reach on port 443. The host reads the TLS name of each connection. *.example.com matches every subdomain and not example.com. An empty list allows no egress. This also ends observe.
- `observe` (boolean): True lets any public TLS name through and records it, so one run of trusted code finds its list. A sandbox with env values answers conflict, and a fork or a snapshot of an observing sandbox answers conflict.

Answers 200 with `Sandbox`.

### egressLog

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/egress/log`

`kiln egress`

Read the egress record: one row per destination, with its decision, counts and bytes. A row names a host, or an address when the connection named no host. A fork or a restore starts with no rows. The rows stay for 7 days after a destroy.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 200 with `EgressLog`.

### egressRequests

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/egress/requests`

`kiln egress-requests`

Read the request log of the bound hosts of one sandbox: method, host, path with no query string, status, binding and time. It holds no header value and no body. It holds at most 10000 rows, and dropped counts the rest. The rows stay for 7 days after a destroy.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 200 with `EgressRequests`.

### exec

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/exec`

`kiln exec`

Run a command inside a sandbox. Accept text/event-stream to read the output as it runs.

This call can stream. Read the body as it arrives.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `cmd` (array of string, required): Command and its arguments.
- `cwd` (string): Directory the command runs in.
- `env` (object): Extra environment variables.
- `timeout_seconds` (integer): Seconds until the command is killed.

Answers 200 with `ExecResult`.

### readFile

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/{path...}`

`kiln files read`

Read one file out of a sandbox. The answer is the file's bytes.

This call can stream. Read the body as it arrives.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `path` (string): Path inside the sandbox.

Answers 200 with `FileBody`.

### writeFile

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/{path...}`

`kiln files write`

Write one file into a sandbox. The request body is the file's bytes, and parent directories are created.

This call can stream. Read the body as it arrives.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `path` (string): Path inside the sandbox.

Answers 204 with no body.

### fork

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/fork`

`kiln sandboxes fork`

Snapshot a running sandbox and restore several copies of it.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `count` (integer, required): Number of copies.
- `allow_secret_fork` (boolean): Allow a fork of a sandbox that holds secrets.
- `point` (string): Timeline point to fork from. The sandbox does not change, and a sleeping one stays asleep. The copies start with the egress policy of the point.
- `credentials` (array of object): Credential bindings of each new sandbox, in the form setCredentials takes. A copy starts with none, and a snapshot holds none.
- `metadata` (object): Metadata of the new sandboxes. It replaces the metadata of the origin sandbox, which they keep without this field.

Answers 201 with `SandboxList`.

### logs

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/logs`

`kiln logs`

Read what the guest kept of the start command output, how the start command ended, and the template build result. A sleeping sandbox wakes first.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 200 with `SandboxLogs`.

### startProcess

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/processes`

`kiln processes start`

Start a detached process and answer once it runs. It has no deadline, it outlives this request, and the sandbox does not sleep while it runs.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `cmd` (array of string, required): Command and its arguments.
- `cwd` (string): Directory the command runs in.
- `env` (object): Extra environment variables.

Answers 201 with `ProcessCreated`.

### signalProcess

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}/processes/{pid}`

`kiln processes signal`

Send a signal to the process group of a detached process. A process that has ended takes no signal, and the call still succeeds.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `pid` (string): Process id from startProcess.

Query:

- `signal` (string): TERM, KILL, INT, HUP, QUIT, USR1 or USR2. Default TERM.

Answers 204 with no body.

### readProcess

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/processes/{pid}`

`kiln processes read`

Read the state of a detached process and its output after each offset. One answer holds at most 1 MiB of each stream, the guest keeps the last 8 MiB, and the answer names the next offsets and the bytes lost.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `pid` (string): Process id from startProcess.

Query:

- `stdout_offset` (integer): Byte of stdout to read from. Default 0.
- `stderr_offset` (integer): Byte of stderr to read from. Default 0.

Answers 200 with `Process`.

### publish

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/publish`

`kiln sandboxes publish`

Serve a guest port on a public hostname.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `port` (integer, required): Port inside the sandbox.
- `visibility` (string, required): public or team.
- `viewer_fork` (boolean): Give each viewer login its own fork of one snapshot of this sandbox. It needs visibility team, and every published port routes to the fork. A later plain publish of this sandbox is a conflict. Retiring any port retires them all, with every fork and the snapshot.
- `viewer_cap` (integer): The most live viewer forks. Required with viewer_fork. A viewer past it gets a page that names the limit.
- `allow_secret_fork` (boolean): Allow viewer forks of a sandbox that holds secrets, because each fork copies that memory.
- `viewer_credentials` (array of object): Credential bindings of each viewer fork, in the form setCredentials takes. A fork starts with none.

Answers 201 with `Published`.

### retire

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}/publish/{port}`

`kiln sandboxes retire`

Retire a published hostname. It answers 404 from then on.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `port` (integer): Published guest port.

Answers 204 with no body.

### snapshot

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/snapshot`

`kiln sandboxes snapshot`

Snapshot a sandbox. With stop the sandbox sleeps and keeps its hostnames.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `stop` (boolean): Stop the sandbox after the snapshot.

Answers 201 with `SnapshotCreated`.

### terminal

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/terminal`

`kiln terminal`

Open an interactive shell in a sandbox over a WebSocket. A binary message carries terminal bytes both ways, and a text message carries {"cols":n,"rows":n}.

This call is a WebSocket upgrade, not a request and an answer. The OpenAPI document and the generated clients leave it out.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `cols` (integer): Terminal width at the moment the shell opens.
- `rows` (integer): Terminal height at the moment the shell opens.

Answers 101 with no body.

### listPoints

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/timeline`

`kiln timeline list`

List the timeline points of one sandbox, oldest first, with id, label, time and bytes. merged counts the older points the limit folded into a point.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Answers 200 with `TimelinePointList`.

### markPoint

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/timeline`

`kiln timeline mark`

Mark a timeline point: memory, processes and disk, held as a diff against the point before it. The guest pauses for the write. The template needs timeline: true, or this answers conflict, as a sandbox that observes egress does. A sandbox holds at most 32 points, and their bytes stay under twice the guest memory plus the disk size. At either limit Kiln merges the two oldest points.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.

Body:

- `label` (string): Name for this point, at most 200 bytes.

Answers 201 with `TimelinePoint`.

### deletePoint

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}/timeline/{point}`

`kiln timeline delete`

Remove one timeline point. Kiln merges its pages into the next point, so the later points still restore.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `point` (string): Point id.

Answers 204 with no body.

### rewindPoint

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/timeline/{point}/rewind`

`kiln timeline rewind`

Stop the guest and restore a timeline point under the same sandbox id and hostnames. Every later point goes, and open connections end. The current egress policy and credential bindings stay. The guest gets new entropy.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id.
- `point` (string): Point id.

Answers 200 with `Sandbox`.

### viewerForks

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/viewer-forks`

`kiln sandboxes viewer-forks`

List each viewer of a viewer fork origin and the id of its live fork.

Path:

- `id` (string): Sandbox id of the origin.

Answers 200 with `ViewerForkList`.

### listSnapshots

`GET /v1/snapshots`

`kiln snapshots list`

List the snapshots of this tenant.

Answers 200 with `SnapshotList`.

### deleteSnapshot

`DELETE /v1/snapshots/{id}`

`kiln snapshots delete`

Delete a snapshot that has no live sandbox.

Path:

- `id` (string): Snapshot id.

Answers 204 with no body.

### getSnapshot

`GET /v1/snapshots/{id}`

`kiln snapshots get`

Read one snapshot.

Path:

- `id` (string): Snapshot id.

Answers 200 with `Snapshot`.

### restore

`POST /v1/snapshots/{id}/restore`

`kiln snapshots restore`

Restore a snapshot into one or more new sandboxes.

Path:

- `id` (string): Snapshot id.

Body:

- `count` (integer, required): Number of sandboxes.
- `allow_secret_fork` (boolean): Allow a restore of a snapshot that holds secrets.
- `credentials` (array of object): Credential bindings of each new sandbox, in the form setCredentials takes. A copy starts with none, and a snapshot holds none.
- `metadata` (object): Metadata of the new sandboxes. It replaces the metadata of the origin sandbox, which they keep without this field.

Answers 201 with `SandboxList`.

### listTemplates

`GET /v1/templates`

`kiln templates list`

List the templates of this tenant.

Answers 200 with `TemplateList`.

### createTemplate

`POST /v1/templates`

`kiln templates create`

Build a template from an OCI image. The build runs after the answer.

Body:

- `name` (string, required): Name of the template inside this tenant.
- `image` (string, required): OCI image reference, for example docker.io/library/python:3.12-slim.
- `vcpus` (integer, required): Virtual CPUs of every sandbox from this template, 1 to 32.
- `memory_mb` (integer, required): Memory of every sandbox from this template.
- `disk_mb` (integer, required): Disk of every sandbox from this template.
- `setup` (array of string): Commands that run once while the template builds.
- `egress_allow` (array of string, required): Hostnames a sandbox may reach. *.example.com matches every subdomain and not example.com. An empty list allows no egress.
- `timeline` (boolean): Let each sandbox of this template take timeline points. Dirty page tracking adds a cost to guest writes, so only a template that uses it pays.
- `ttl_seconds` (integer): Seconds until the host deletes this template with its snapshot and its sandboxes. A preview environment sets one, because nothing comes back to delete it.
- `start` (array of string): Command that runs the application. Kiln ignores what the image says to run, so a template that serves an application names this. It runs once, when a sandbox restores from this template.
- `port` (integer): Port the application listens on. Creating a sandbox answers only once the guest accepts a connection there. Required with start. With no start, the application runs the command its image names.
- `services` (array of object): Images that run beside the application in one microVM, started in order before the template snapshot, so every sandbox restores with them running. Each has name, image, and optional env, port, start and ready. The name resolves to 127.0.0.1 in every root. port and ready decide when the next service starts. No service is published unless a caller publishes its port.
- `seed` (array of string): Commands that run in the application root after every service is ready and before the template snapshot, such as migrations.
- `user` (string): User from the image, by name or numeric id. Exec, detached processes, files, the terminal and the start command run as this user, and setup runs as root. Empty runs everything as root. The build fails when the image has no such user. In a sandbox the user owns the cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/user, with the cpu, memory, pids and io controllers, and its processes start in /sys/fs/cgroup/user/init. It also owns /var/lib/kiln-data, a directory on the sandbox disk outside the overlay root, so rootless Docker can use it as its data-root with the overlay2 driver. That directory is in every snapshot and fork, and it shares disk_mb with the rest of the sandbox.
- `credential` (object): Registry login for this build only: username and token. It pulls from the registry of the image, the host keeps it in memory for the build, and it is never returned. Without it the build uses the stored credentials of this tenant.

Answers 202 with `TemplateState`.

### deleteTemplate

`DELETE /v1/templates/{name}`

`kiln templates delete`

Delete a template that has no live sandbox and no snapshot.

Path:

- `name` (string): Name of the template.

Answers 204 with no body.

### getTemplate

`GET /v1/templates/{name}`

`kiln templates get`

Read one template.

Path:

- `name` (string): Name of the template.

Answers 200 with `Template`.

### listViewers

`GET /v1/viewers`

`kiln viewers list`

List the viewers of this tenant.

Answers 200 with `ViewerList`.

### createViewer

`POST /v1/viewers`

`kiln viewers create`

Add a viewer of this tenant. A viewer opens team previews and nothing else.

Body:

- `email` (string, required): Address the viewer signs in with.
- `password` (string, required): Password of the viewer.

Answers 201 with `Viewer`.

### deleteViewer

`DELETE /v1/viewers/{id}`

`kiln viewers delete`

Revoke one viewer. The viewer is disabled and its sessions end.

Path:

- `id` (string): Viewer id.

Answers 204 with no body.
